name: Question 10
problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(5,3,7)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨-2,-3,6⟩=16.$
worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,-3,6⟩ & =16 \\ -2x-3y+6z & =16 \\ 2x & =6z-3y-16 \\ x & =3z-\frac{3}{2}y-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $y=2$ and $z=1,$ we get 

$$
x=3-\frac{3}{2}(2)-8=-8.
$$

So, the point $Q(-8,2,1)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-8,2,1⟩-⟨5,3,7⟩ \\  & =⟨-13,-1,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-2,-3,6⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-13)\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot (-3)+(-6)\cdot 6|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|26+3-36|}{\sqrt{4+9+36}} \\  & =\frac{|-7|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{7}{7} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we need to find a point on the plane. If r=⟨x,y,z⟩, we obtain

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨−2,−3,6⟩=16−2x−3y+6z=162x=6z−3y−16x=3z−32y−8.

Setting y=2 and z=1, we get

x=3−32(2)−8=−8.

So, the point Q(−8,2,1) lies on the plane.

Now, we find

PQ→=⟨−8,2,1⟩−⟨5,3,7⟩=⟨−13,−1,−6⟩.

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector n=⟨−2,−3,6⟩.

Finally, the shortest distance from the point P to the plane Π is the absolute value of the scalar projection of PQ→ onto the normal vector of the plane:

d=|compnPQ→|=|PQ→⋅n||n|=|(−13)⋅(−2)+(−1)⋅(−3)+(−6)⋅6|(−2)2+(−3)2+62=|26+3−36|4+9+36=|−7|49=77=1.
